Report · 2026-08-27 representation

Complex representation analysis

Following Figure 6 of the co-folding representation study (Boltz2-as-FM, arXiv:2602.13249): how does our pretrained density-ViT encoder relate to other protein–ligand complex encoders? We test four angles on the same 1320 LP-PDBbind (lp_edrscc_v2) test complexes: (1) how aligned the representation spaces are, (2) whether they are complementary for affinity, (3) whether our density-conditioned encoder carries richer information — its representation reconstructs and stitches into the others while resisting the reverse — and (4) label-light quality / information metrics from recent ML work (effective rank, intrinsic dimension, 𝒱-usable information).

Key findings
  • Distinct space (§1). Our two density encoders are each other's closest match (CKA 0.58) yet sit apart from every external complex encoder (CKA 0.05–0.20) — a distinct representation region.
  • Complementary (§2). Concatenating a less-aligned encoder gives the largest affinity gain (AEV-PLIG: Δρ +0.035 over ours alone).
  • Richer, and quantified (§3). Against a same-recipe seed-twin ceiling, another CDG recovers 100% of it but coordinates recover only 67% — so ~33% of CDG's information is density-unique (unreconstructable from coordinates).
  • Information & geometry (§4). Density lifts effective rank (163→178) and intrinsic dimension (8.9→12.0), and adds +0.022 nats of usable affinity information (helping 58% of complexes).
  • Takeaway. Electron density yields a richer, higher-dimensional, distinct complex representation; the affinity-usable increment is real but modest.

  • CKNNA / CKA: features are column-centred then row-L2-normalised; CKNNA follows the minyoungg/platonic-rep reference (unbiased HSIC on the mutual-k-NN masked kernel).
  • Encoders: Ours = frozen density-ViT patch-token mean-pool (640-d); ProFSA = frozen [mol;pocket] head input; GET / AEV-PLIG = pooled graph vector (seed0, supervised); DSMBind = mean-pooled all-atom encoder + energy (zero-shot).
  • Caveat: GET and AEV-PLIG are supervised on the LP train split, so their reps are already affinity-tuned; ProFSA (frozen) and DSMBind (zero-shot) are cleaner complementarity tests. The probe is a representation diagnostic (uniform CV on shared test complexes), not the train→test leaderboard number. The alignment→gain trend holds among strong encoders; the weakest (DSMBind) does not help, so the gain reflects alignment × encoder quality, not alignment alone.

3Information richness: cross-representation decodability & stitching

Does one encoder's representation contain another's? Following model stitching (Bansal et al., NeurIPS 2021; Lenc & Vedaldi, CVPR 2015) and its "more-is-better" asymmetry, we fit a low-capacity 2-layer MLP connector to reconstruct each target representation from each source (held-out 5-fold R²). A representation is richer if it reconstructs others well yet is itself hard to reconstruct. We then ground this in the affinity task (functional stitching), and add a training-free check via relative representations (Moschella et al., ICLR 2023 Oral).

3.1Reconstruction R² & richness ranking

Held-out variance-weighted R² of a 2-layer MLP mapping source (row) → target (column). A rich source reconstructs others (high row) while resisting reconstruction (low column). The richness score = meanj[R²(i→j) − R²(j→i)] ranks encoders by net subsumption; higher = contains more of the others' information. (This aggregate score is confounded by target dimensionality — §3.4 gives a ceiling-normalized, confound-free quantification of the density-unique information.)

3.2Functional stitching into the affinity head

Map source → CDG latent with the MLP connector, then read out pK with CDG's own ridge affinity head (Spearman ρ, 5-fold CV). If a source can be stitched up to CDG's own score (ρ = 0.666) it already carried CDG's affinity-relevant information; the residual gap = CDG-unique information. CDG→X is the reverse (CDG stitched into X's head).

3.3Relative-representation zero-shot stitching

Training-free (Moschella et al., ICLR 2023): re-express every complex by its cosine similarity to 256 shared anchor complexes, then train an affinity head on CDG's relative rep and apply it zero-shot to each encoder's relative rep (same anchors → shared coordinates). High sim-to-CDG = near-isometric to CDG; a large drop from CDG's own zero-shot ρ means the space does not communicate with CDG (distinct information).

3.4Seed-twin ceiling: density-unique information

Raw reconstruction R² confounds genuinely unique information with mere target complexity. To divide that out we set a ceiling = reconstruction R² between two CDG models that differ only in random seed (same 100M recipe) — the best achievable when the information is identical (ceiling R² = 0.926). Normalized recovery = R²(X→CDG) / ceiling is the fraction of CDG's recoverable information captured by source X; 1 − normalized is what X cannot reconstruct. For coords-only this residual is exactly the density-unique information: 33% of CDG's reconstructable information is not present in coordinates (an independently-seeded CDG recovers the ceiling, another CDG config recovers near it, coords falls well short).

  • Connector: 2-layer MLP (Linear→GELU→Linear, hidden 384, weight-decay 1e-4, early-stopped), the low-capacity stitching map of Bansal et al. Source and target are per-dim standardised; R² is held-out variance-weighted (5-fold).
  • Reading richness: CDG reconstructs coords-only C better than C reconstructs CDG (positive asymmetry) ⇒ the density channels add information not recoverable from coordinates. The richness bar ranks all six encoders by net decodability asymmetry.
  • Seed-twin ceiling (§3.4): the reference CDG target is a 100M CDG (d640L18h10, seed s1); the ceiling is R²(seed s2 → s1) — same recipe, different init — averaged over both directions. Normalizing by it removes the target-complexity confound so the coords residual is a clean estimate of density-unique information.
  • References: model stitching — Lenc & Vedaldi (CVPR 2015), Bansal, Nakkiran & Barak (NeurIPS 2021); relative representations / zero-shot latent communication — Moschella et al. (ICLR 2023 Oral, arXiv:2209.15430).

4.1Effective rank, intrinsic dimension, task rank

RankMe (Garrido et al., ICML 2023) = exp(entropy of singular values): over how many dimensions variance spreads (label-free richness). TwoNN intrinsic dimension (Valeriani et al., NeurIPS 2023). LiDAR (Thilak et al., ICLR 2024, adapted with pK-quantile classes) = effective rank of the affinity-discriminative directions. Caveat: RankMe/ID are bounded by feature dimension, so read our C vs C+D+G (both 640-d) directly; cross-encoder values are only indicative.

4.2𝒱-usable information about affinity

Predictive 𝒱-information (Ethayarajh et al., ICML 2022; Xu et al., ICLR 2020) = ½·ln(Var(pK)/MSE) under a ridge family — the usable information a representation carries about pK. Our C+D+G carries +0.022 nats more usable affinity information than coords, and the pointwise view shows density adds usable information on 58% of complexes (mean Δpvi = +0.022 nats).

4.3Platonic convergence

The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (Huh et al., ICML 2024) argues strong models converge to a shared representation (measured by the mutual-k-NN / CKNNA alignment used in §1). Mean CKA to the other encoders quantifies how "on-manifold" each encoder is: the supervised structure encoders sit together, while our density encoder is among the least convergent — a distinct, complementary region rather than the shared one.

  • Cross-encoder caveat: RankMe and intrinsic dimension are capped by feature dimensionality (GET 64-d, AEV-PLIG 1536-d), so the same-dimension C vs C+D+G contrast is the controlled comparison; 𝒱-info and LiDAR are dimension-robust (fixed target / bounded by #classes).
  • References: RankMe — Garrido et al. (ICML 2023); LiDAR — Thilak et al. (ICLR 2024); intrinsic dimension / representation geometry — Valeriani et al. (NeurIPS 2023); 𝒱-usable information — Ethayarajh et al. (ICML 2022), Xu et al. (ICLR 2020); Platonic Representation Hypothesis — Huh et al. (ICML 2024).
